title: Update a nested value
description:
Write `updateIn(obj, path, fn)` that returns a **new** object where the value at `path` (an array of keys) is replaced by `fn(oldValue)`. Nothing in `obj` is changed, objects on the path are copied, and everything else is shared:

```javascript
const state = { user: { name: "Ada", stats: { level: 3 } }, items: [] };
const next = updateIn(state, ["user", "stats", "level"], n => n + 1);
next.user.stats.level     // 4
state.user.stats.level    // 3
next.items === state.items   // true
```

Arrays on the path are copied as arrays (numeric keys). A missing object on the path is created as `{}`. An empty path returns `fn(obj)`.
hints: Recursion fits: to update `path` in `obj`, update `path.slice(1)` in `obj[path[0]]`, then return a copy of `obj` with that one key replaced (lesson 8.05).
`{ ...current, [key]: child }` copies an object with one key changed; for arrays, `slice()` and then set the index.
